crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Drafting Proposal Responses
children.blurb: Drafting proposal responses covers the work of turning a request for proposal, request for information, or security questionnaire into a structured draft answer.

children.name: Agent Negotiation in Over-the-Counter Markets
children.blurb: Agent negotiation in over-the-counter markets covers software agents that quote, counterquote, and agree terms for instruments traded bilaterally rather than on a central limit order book.

children.name: Investment Committee Memos
children.blurb: Investment committee memos are the formal documents that lay out a proposed investment, the supporting evidence, the risks, and a recommendation for a committee to decide on.

children.name: Keeping Comparable Company Sets Current
children.blurb: Keeping comparable company sets current is the work of maintaining a peer group used for valuation, benchmarking, and relative performance analysis as companies change.

children.name: Automating Trade Settlement
children.blurb: Automating trade settlement covers the post-trade steps that move a trade from execution to final exchange of cash and securities, including trade matching, confirmation, reconciliation, settlement instruction generation, and exception handling.

sections.body: Agent workflows in finance use AI systems to carry out multi-step tasks that once required analysts, lawyers, and operations staff. In practice, these agents read documents, extract terms, draft text, compare data, and pass work to other agents or humans. For proposal responses, an agent can assemble prior answers, check requirements, and produce a first draft for review. In over-the-counter markets, agents can quote, counter, and log negotiation positions, though final authority usually stays with a person. Investment committee memos and comparable company updates are similar: the agent gathers inputs, writes a structured summary, and flags missing evidence. Settlement is more mechanical, with agents matching trades, checking instructions, and escalating exceptions.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are genuinely automated, especially document assembly, data refresh, and routine settlement matching. Other parts remain supervised, because negotiation, valuation judgment, and memo conclusions carry consequences that firms are not ready to delegate. The hard limits are data quality, audit trails, and the fact that financial language is often ambiguous or deliberately vague. An agent can draft a proposal response but cannot know whether a client will accept a term, and it can update a comparable set but cannot decide which peer is truly comparable. Settlement automation is constrained by legacy systems, cut-off times, and regulatory reporting, not by the model alone. The site's 355 merger and acquisition filings show how often comparable company sets need revision, which is a recurring maintenance problem rather than a one-time task.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section follow the workflow from pitch to post-trade. Drafting Proposal Responses covers the front end, where an agent turns a request into a structured answer. Agent Negotiation in Over-the-Counter Markets deals with the interactive middle, where quotes and counteroffers are exchanged and recorded. Investment Committee Memos is where the agent assembles evidence and arguments for a decision meeting. Keeping Comparable Company Sets Current addresses the ongoing data work that supports valuation and memo writing. Automating Trade Settlement covers the back end, where matched trades become final transfers and exceptions are routed. A reader can move through these pages in order or jump to the stage that matches their own process.
